1 

 Order 
This writ petition has been filed challenging the order passed by the first respondent dated 19.12.2016, thereby rejected the request made by the petitioner seeking permission to transport his elephant. 
2. Heard the learned counsel on either side and perused the materials placed before this Court.
3. The petitioner owns elephant and he used to transport it for temple festivals during Hindu rituals. 
Therefore, the petitioner applied before the respondents seeking for permission to transport his elephant. However it was rejected on various grounds. 
4. A perusal of the counter filed by the first respondent revealed that the elephants' owners have applied for transportation of their https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis elephants to long distance frequently. They used to transport their elephants without giving enough rest to the elephants between functions and also without following the Tamil Nadu Captive Elephants (Management and Maintenance) Rules, 2011. Therefore, in order to avoid cruel act meted out to the captive elephants by the elephant owners in maintaining and treating the elephants and to regulate the method of transporting captive elephants and their work in functions in proper way, certain guidelines have been framed under the aforesaid Rules. On 19.12.2016, the following guidelines are issued by the first respondent hereunder:-
i. The Transit period for the captive elephant is restricted to maximum 15 days to transport from the place of the owner to another place. As per the Tamil Nadu Captive Elephants (Management and Maintenance) Rules 2011, the elephant should be returned to the elephant owners place and enough rest given after completion of one transit period. 
ii. The elephant owners should apply for a fresh transit permit only 10 days after completion of the period of previous permit. 
iii. While transporting the elephant to the religious/temple functions, shortest route should be used and are not https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis permitted to longest route.
iv. While applying transit permit in respect of temple functions, the elephant owner should attach an authorized letter obtained from the temple authorities. If not, the permission will be rejected. If the function is cancelled after obtaining the permit, it will not be permitted to participate in another function on the same date. No permission will be granted for marriage functions considering the safety of the public and the panic situation that is usually present. v. While participating a function for 3 or more than 3 days, an authorization letter regarding the provision of basic needs (food, water and residence) to the elephant should have already been obtained from the function organizers and enclosed with the application form submitted by the R.Rengan vs / on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176126964/
2 elephant owners. 
vi. There should be two days interval in between two functions for which one permit is issued. vii. The application for transit permit should reach this office before 15 days before the date of function/festivals. viii. Health certificate for the elephant for transportation should be obtained only from the Government Veterinary Assistant Surgeons. 
ix. The demand draft for the required fee in favour of Principal Chief Conservator of Forests should have been obtained from the nationalised bank before one week of the date of application. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis x. Transit permit will not be issued to the elephant owner to participate in the places that are coming under Corporation limit. 
5. Thus, the petitioner was rightly directed to apply afresh as per the aforesaid Rules and this Court finds no infirmity or illegality in the impugned order passed by the first respondent. This writ petition is dismissed accordingly. However the petitioner is at liberty to apply afresh following the guidelines issued by the first respondent. No costs. 
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
